title: User guide 4: Animated slides
bullets: Slides that build up as the narrator speaks
Layouts for steps, equations, cycles and comparisons
subtitle: User guide 4: Animated slides
narration: Welcome to user guide four. Videos are now made with animated slides. Items appear one by one, exactly when the narrator reaches them, and the item being spoken is highlighted. This guide shows the layouts, and how to ask for them.

subtitle: Default: bullet points appear one by one
narration: By default, the short points of a slide appear one by one as the narrator reaches them. The current point is bold, and the earlier points stay on screen. The headline slides in at the start, and each slide fades into the next.

subtitle: Flow: steps with arrows
narration: The flow layout shows two to five steps. Each step appears when it is spoken, and an arrow is drawn to the next one. Use it for a procedure, like a science experiment, or for inputs, process and outputs.

subtitle: Equation: terms appear in order
narration: The equation layout builds a formula one term at a time. Inputs and outputs have different colours, and a short note can appear underneath. It suits chemical or word equations, like the one for photosynthesis.

subtitle: Cycle: nodes in a loop
narration: The cycle layout puts three to six nodes in a loop, and draws the arrows around it. Use it for the water cycle, the life cycle of a butterfly, or any process that repeats.

subtitle: Compare: two columns
narration: The compare layout shows two columns side by side, each with a title and up to four points. Use it to compare two things, like autotrophs and heterotrophs.

title: How to ask for a layout
bullets: You do nothing special: the ChatGPT prompt already asks for the layouts
In lesson_plan.json, each slide may have a layout and a diagram
Keep labels short: one to four words, in the lesson language
List the items in the order the narrator says them
If a diagram is wrong, the import check tells you which slide and why
subtitle: How to ask for a layout
narration: You don't have to do anything special. The prompt in the app already asks ChatGPT for a layout for each slide, in the lesson plan file. If you edit it yourself, keep the labels short, and list the items in the order the narrator says them. If a diagram is not valid, the import check tells you which slide has the problem and why.

title: Where to choose it
bullets: Make the video, Slides: Animated (recommended) or Plain
Timing is matched to the narration length, not to individual words
Next: pictures and richer illustrations come in a later release
subtitle: Where to choose it
narration: In the Make the video step, the Slides choice is animated by default, or plain if you prefer still slides. The timing follows the narration length sentence by sentence, not word by word. Pictures and richer illustrations are planned for a later release.
